This is meant for a smart 5-year-old with a loose understanding of the stock exchange, interest rates, the former gold standard, and currency.

If they could be nearly equated to gold miners, bitcoin miners have machinery and operating costs because it takes time and effort to find bitcoins. They have to sell their bitcoins at the best price they can get, but they would be reluctant to sell at a loss. So, you are paying for their work in a sense.

Exchanges may try to manipulate prices, or at least prospectors, who have invested in bitcoin and operate through the exchange, try to. Also, mining conglomerates have become a thing, so manipulation of the market can easily occur, but this isn't much different from the diamond industry.

Ultimately, people only buy, sell, or trade anything of value because they think they can get something of value in turn and this happens universally. So, the exchange price you see is generally a reflection of that. You could be buying from a miner or some other investor at the exchange. They want to convert some of their bitcoin to make a profit or spend it outside of the bitcoin ecosystem. Merchants could be interacting with an exchange in some way after selling their goods for bitcoin. They usually do not want to keep all of their profits in bitcoin.

Merchant services also have a great effect on the market just as a company like Visa does with their control of purchasing power. The specifics of this get hard to detail, but let's not get into that. As you know, merchants can set the price of their goods to any value depending on what people will pay. Yet, they aren't usually treating bitcoin independently of fiat currency (the US dollar). They are setting bitcoin prices for what they can get in the BTC -> USD conversion.

So, to understand the basics of bitcoin, you should understand how the aforementioned groups are making their profits, that is, bitcoin miners with their hardware investment, prospectors and various parties with their direct investment at the exchanges, and merchants with their product investment.
